sentences.zh: 乔治·哈里森，你知道的，他对灵性非常感兴趣，对天主教的灵性很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And in money.
sentences.zh: 还有钱。

sentences.en: He's certainly interested in money as well.
sentences.zh: 他当然也对钱感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Complaining about the tax man.
sentences.zh: 抱怨税务官。

sentences.en: And they come to see Christianity as boring, because Christianity in 1960s Britain is boring.
sentences.zh: 他们开始觉得基督教很无聊，因为1960年代英国的基督教就是很无聊。

sentences.en: It's stale, it's dull, it's associated with hierarchy, it's losing its self-confidence.
sentences.zh: 它陈腐、枯燥、与等级制度挂钩，正在失去自信。

sentences.en: This is, you know, the period where people in the church are saying they don't believe in God.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是教会里的人开始说他们不相信上帝的时期。

sentences.en: Honest to God and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 《诚实对上帝》以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And so that's why I think it's perfectly reasonable for John Lennon to say that they're bigger than Jesus.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我认为约翰·列侬说他们比耶稣更受欢迎是完全合情合理的。

sentences.en: They certainly are in England.
sentences.zh: 他们在英国确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think that they have absorbed a lot of Christian assumptions.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们吸收了许多基督教的假设。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the key message of, you know, peace and love, which even Ringo says all the time, peace and love.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，和平与爱的核心信息——连林戈也整天挂在嘴边，和平与爱。

sentences.en: These are basically Christian ideals.
sentences.zh: 这些基本上都是基督教的理想。

sentences.en: And all you need is love.
sentences.zh: 还有你所需要的就是爱。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an enduring Christian message.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个持久的基督教信息。

sentences.en: And the fact that they sing all you need is love as their contribution to a global festival of culture.
sentences.zh: 他们演唱《All You Need Is Love》作为对全球文化节日的贡献，这一事实本身就很说明问题。

sentences.en: You know, all these satellites around the world joining people up from around countries around the entire globe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，全世界所有的卫星将来自全球各个国家的人们连接在一起。

sentences.en: And the Beatles singing all you need is love.
sentences.zh: 而披头士在歌唱《All You Need Is Love》。

sentences.en: It's Britain's contribution to what they see as a kind of universal message.
sentences.zh: 这是英国对他们所认为的一种普遍信息的贡献。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it draws on pretty fundamental Christian ideas.
sentences.zh: 但这借鉴了相当基础的基督教思想。

sentences.en: But the problem is because Christianity, its image is so boring and dull and staid, the Beatles are not interested in that.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，因为基督教的形象太无聊、太沉闷、太古板了，披头士对此毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: And so the Maharishi kind of provides that.
sentences.zh: 所以马哈里希恰好提供了这一点。

sentences.en: And the Maharishi, you know, he's packaging his message for Western tastes.
sentences.zh: 而且马哈里希，你知道的，他把自己的信息包装成迎合西方审美的样子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Rather in the way that, you know, Indian food is packaged for British tastes.
sentences.zh: 就像印度菜被包装成迎合英国人的口味一样。

sentences.en: He's the chicken tikka masala of gurus.
sentences.zh: 他就是大师中的“鸡胸肉玛莎拉”。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the chicken tikka masala of mid-60s spirituality.
sentences.zh: 对，他就是60年代中期灵性界的鸡胸肉玛莎拉。

sentences.en: And, you know, George Harrison is kind of, I guess, the archetype of this.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，乔治·哈里森可以说是这方面的典型代表。

sentences.en: Because he remains a very Catholic kind of Hindu.
sentences.zh: 因为他始终是一个非常天主教式的印度教徒。

sentences.en: And the way in which My Sweet Lord, the smash hit that he releases after the Beatles have broken up,
sentences.zh: 以及他在披头士解散后发行的轰动一时的热门单曲《My Sweet Lord》中展现的那种方式，

sentences.en: the chorus goes from, you know, hallelujah, hallelujah, to hari Krishna, hari Krishna.
sentences.zh: 副歌的部分，从哈利路亚、哈利路亚，变成了哈瑞·奎师那、哈瑞·奎师那。

sentences.en: But it sounds exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 但听起来完全一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that they are, again, they're kind of, they're both representative and influential on what seems to me a pretty fundamental trend,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，他们再次体现了并影响了一种在我看来相当根本的趋势，

sentences.en: certainly here in Britain, that, you know, the guiding assumption now of our elites is that all religions are basically the same.
sentences.zh: 当然是在英国，我们精英阶层的指导假设现在是，所有宗教基本上都是一样的。

sentences.en: Surely they all teach you peace and love and basic fundamentals.
sentences.zh: 它们肯定都教导你和平、爱以及最基本的原则。

sentences.en: And I think that the role the Beatles play in that is fairly hefty.
sentences.zh: 我认为披头士乐队在其中扮演的角色相当分量重。

sentences.en: Was that turning into a bit of a Paul McCartney-ish impersonation there when you said people?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说“人们”的时候，是在模仿保罗·麦卡特尼吗？

sentences.en: I didn't notice it, but if it was, it may be.
sentences.zh: 我没注意到，但如果是的话，那可能吧。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the Beatles and their wealth and celebrity.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈披头士乐队以及他们的财富和名气。

sentences.en: So I'm trying to think if there have been people...
sentences.zh: 所以我在想要是以前有人……

sentences.en: Imagine no possessions.
sentences.zh: 想象没有财产。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: John Lennon, his massive house in, where is it, Weybridge?
sentences.zh: 约翰·列侬，他在韦布里奇的巨型宅邸，在哪里来着？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: St. George's Hill, where the Diggers had tried to set up their commune in the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 圣乔治山，17世纪时掘地派曾试图在那里建立公社的地方。

sentences.en: And it's now a gated community, and I've tried to go and visit it so many times, and every time I get turned away by Russian bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 而现在它成了一个封闭式社区，我试过很多次去参观，每次都被俄罗斯保镖挡在门外。

sentences.en: Both Wynne Stanley and John Lennon were, you know, turning in their graves.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿·丘吉尔和约翰·列侬大概都要在棺材里气得翻身了。

sentences.en: It's strange that you have nothing else to do, Tom, than hang around outside the gates of other people's houses.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，除了在别人家门外闲晃，你好像无所事事，这挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: Well, I do, but, you know, periodically I try and get to see it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有事要做，但你知道，我隔一段时间就会想去看看。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to think if there are people before the Beatles in British, certainly British cultural history,
sentences.zh: 但我在想，在英国——至少是英国文化史上，在披头士之前，

sentences.en: who had either the international fame or the amount of money overnight that they did.
sentences.zh: 有没有人能在一夜之间拥有他们那样国际化的名声或巨额财富。

sentences.en: And I think that's another, to me, that's another obvious area where they're pioneers, where it's hard to...
sentences.zh: 我认为这是另一个显而易见的领域，对我来说，他们是先驱，很难……

sentences.en: So this is why, I mean, what they do is they do what entrepreneurs and manufacturers would have done 100 years earlier, which is they buy country houses.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，我的意思是，他们的做法就像100年前的企业家和制造商会做的那样，那就是买乡村别墅。

sentences.en: It's interesting that they haven't freed themselves from the shackles of their Britishness.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他们并没有让自己摆脱英国人身份的枷锁。

sentences.en: So their instinct is immediately, I mean, Lennon and, I think, George, they buy these stockbroker-built houses, and then they go into the bigger sort of national trust style.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的直觉马上就是——我是说列侬和乔治吧，他们买下这些股票经纪人风格建造的房子，然后他们才进入那种更大规模的国民信托风格。

sentences.en: But Paul McCartney doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但保罗·麦卡特尼没有。

sentences.en: No, that's what makes him interesting.
sentences.zh: 对，这正是他的有趣之处。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is Paul McCartney, who's always seen as the kind of the more conventional of Lennon and McCartney, is actually much more interested in the avant-garde,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，一直被视为列侬和麦卡特尼中更传统的那一个保罗·麦卡特尼，其实对前卫艺术更感兴趣，

sentences.en: and is at the heart of swinging London when it's at its most swinging.
sentences.zh: 并且处在摇摆伦敦最摇摆时期的核心。

sentences.en: Well, that's because of his association.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为他的社交圈子。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an interesting thing about class, because McCartney has an in with the Asher family,
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于阶级，这是一个有趣的现象，因为麦卡特尼能接触到阿舍尔家族，

sentences.en: which is a very well-connected, patrician, culturally-connected family through his relationship with Jane Asher.
sentences.zh: 这是一个背景深厚、具有贵族气派且文化联系紧密的家族，通过他与简·阿舍尔的关系。

sentences.en: He basically moves in with her, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他基本上搬去和她一起住了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's how he discovers stock housing and all this sort of business.
sentences.zh: 这就是他如何发现伦敦市区的房子以及所有这类事情的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But I think what's interesting about them is that they are...
sentences.zh: 但我觉得他们有趣的地方在于，他们是……

sentences.en: They're a new kind of sort of elite that Britain had not previously produced.
sentences.zh: 他们是英国以前从未产生过的一种新精英。

sentences.en: So Dickens wasn't unmoored from his society in the way that they are to become later on.
sentences.zh: 所以狄更斯并没有像他们后来那样与社会脱节。

sentences.en: Do you not think?
sentences.zh: 你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 不，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: And I think that that's what makes particularly John and Yoko interesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这一点让约翰和小野洋子特别有趣。

sentences.en: Because obviously...
sentences.zh: 因为很明显……

sentences.en: The Harry and Meghan of the 1960s.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代的哈里和梅根。

sentences.en: The Harry and Meghan of the 60s.
sentences.zh: 60年代的哈里和梅根。

sentences.en: It's evident that John Lennon living in his stockbroke about house is desperately unhappy because he's lonely and bored and he doesn't know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 很明显，约翰·列侬住在他的股票经纪人风格豪宅里，感到极其痛苦，因为他孤独、无聊，又不知道该拿它怎么办。

sentences.en: And he is kind of deracinated, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而且他有点无根无基，我猜。

sentences.en: I mean, he's lost his roots.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他失去了根基。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so he's looking for something else.
sentences.zh: 所以他在寻找别的东西。

sentences.en: And his relationship with Yoko, I mean, symbolized by his replacing Winston as his middle name with Ono.
sentences.zh: 他与洋子的关系，我的意思是，象征意义就是他把中间名温斯顿换成了小野。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite a...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这相当……

sentences.en: It's kind of wonderfully culturally symbolic.
sentences.zh: 这在文化象征意义上非常奇妙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But he blazes a path that many people have followed now.
sentences.zh: 但他开辟了一条现在许多人都效仿的道路。

sentences.en: And you could say that the whole...
sentences.zh: 你可以说整个……

sentences.en: He blazes a path that is currently convulsing the nation, I think.
sentences.zh: 他开辟了一条目前正在震撼整个国家的道路，我认为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, Lennon's an interesting one, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 我是说，列侬是个很有意思的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he basically...
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上……

sentences.en: I mean, ironically, having said the Beatles were bigger than Jesus, he then decides to dress like Jesus.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，在说过披头士比耶稣更受欢迎之后，他接着决定把自己打扮得像耶稣。

sentences.en: He does, yes.
sentences.zh: 他是这么做了，是的。

sentences.en: And to look like Jesus.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来就像耶稣。

sentences.en: And his sort of role...
sentences.zh: 他那种角色……

sentences.en: I mean, he definitely sees himself...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他绝对把自己视为……

sentences.en: I mean, he would love your thesis.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他会很喜欢你的论点。

sentences.en: Because your thesis is how he thinks of himself, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你的论点正是他如何看待自己的，对吧？

sentences.en: As a moral prophet rather than as a musician.
sentences.zh: 把自己当作一个道德先知，而不是音乐家。

sentences.en: But do you think that sort of moral prophecy still has force all these years on?
sentences.zh: 但你认为这种道德预言在多年后还有力量吗？

sentences.en: I mean, do you think young people give a damn about John Lennon now?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你认为现在的年轻人还在乎约翰·列侬吗？

sentences.en: I don't think they give a damn about John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他们在乎约翰·列侬。

sentences.en: But I think the way in which he set himself up as a kind of holy fool, the way in which he deliberately sought to trash things that people held sacred.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他把自己包装成一种神圣的傻瓜的方式，他刻意寻求摧毁人们视为神圣的事物的方式。

sentences.en: So I watched...
sentences.zh: 所以我看了……

sentences.en: Dorian Linsky was here at the festival yesterday talking about protest songs.
sentences.zh: 多利安·林斯基昨天在音乐节上谈论抗议歌曲。

sentences.en: And he made the kind of wonderful point that John Lennon's protest songs are basically lists of things that he doesn't agree with.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一个绝妙的观点，即约翰·列侬的抗议歌曲基本上就是他不同意的事情的清单。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That he doesn't like.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢的那些事。

sentences.en: And there's the song God on his first solo album, where he goes through all the things that he had previously valued and now he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 在他的第一张个人专辑里有一首歌叫《上帝》，他在歌中数落了他以前珍视现在却不再珍视的所有东西。

sentences.en: So he famously says, I don't believe in Beatles.
sentences.zh: 所以他有句名言，我不相信披头士。

sentences.en: But he also says, I don't believe in God.
sentences.zh: 但他也说，我不相信上帝。

sentences.en: I don't believe in Jesus.
sentences.zh: 我不相信耶稣。

sentences.en: I don't believe in Buddha.
sentences.zh: 我不相信佛陀。

sentences.en: I don't believe in yoga.
sentences.zh: 我不相信瑜伽。

sentences.en: So basically, he is...
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他是……

sentences.en: The way in which you get cultural capital by trashing things that people hold sacred seems to me quite significant.
sentences.zh: 通过贬低人们视为神圣的事物来获得文化资本的方式，在我看来相当重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because that's what we're living through at the moment.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是我们目前正在经历的生活。

sentences.en: And he really does seem to me a trailblazer there.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他确实是一个开创者。

sentences.en: There's a story, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 有个故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Elton John went to visit him in New York and saw John Lennon getting very cross because one of the golden doorknobs had come off in an apartment or something.
sentences.zh: 埃尔顿·约翰去纽约拜访他，看到约翰·列侬因为公寓里一个金色门把手掉下来或者别的什么而大发雷霆。

sentences.en: And Elton says to him, imagine no possessions, John.
sentences.zh: 埃尔顿对他说，想象没有财产，约翰。

sentences.en: And John says, it's only an effing song.
sentences.zh: 约翰说，这只是一首该死的歌。

sentences.en: Quite.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Quite.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Because I think that the hypocrisy is also a crucial part of it.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为虚伪也是其中至关重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And that also is a massive part of the tension that the cultural revolution that we're going through is having to wrestle with.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们正在经历的文化革命不得不应对的巨大紧张关系的一部分。

sentences.en: Because you've got people who are casting down the statues, but then filming it on their iPhones, which are made from materials that have been sourced by basically slaves.
sentences.zh: 因为你有这样的人，他们在推倒雕像，但随后用他们的iPhone拍摄下来，而这些iPhone的材料基本上是由奴隶开采出来的。

sentences.en: So the hypocrisy there is also, you know, John Lennon and Yoko Ono, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以其中的虚伪也是，你知道的，约翰·列侬和小野洋子，你知道的，

sentences.en: that they're in their hotel room and they have to stop their protest because the chambermate has to come in and make their bed.
sentences.zh: 他们在酒店房间里，却不得不暂停抗议，因为客房服务员必须进来整理床铺。

sentences.en: Yeah, I always like that detail.
sentences.zh: 对，我一直很喜欢这个细节。

sentences.en: That's their bed in, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是他们的“床上抗议”，对吧？

sentences.en: That's their bed in, in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 那是他们在阿姆斯特丹的“床上抗议”。

sentences.en: So I think, I mean, I think he's, I think John Lennon in particular will be a subject of great fascination to future historians.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，我的意思是，我认为他，我认为尤其是约翰·列侬将会成为未来历史学家深感兴趣的主题。

sentences.en: I mean, do you not think so?
sentences.zh: 我是说，难道你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Well, I've written about John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我写过关于约翰·列侬的文章。

sentences.en: I mean, I've never had worse feedback than when I've written about John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我写约翰·列侬时受到的反馈从来没有这么糟糕过。

sentences.en: Because as you know, I don't really hold a candle for John Lennon.
sentences.zh: 因为如你所知，我其实并不怎么支持约翰·列侬。

sentences.en: Is that morally or musically or?
sentences.zh: 那是从道德上、音乐上还是别的什么？

sentences.en: Sort of, he's everything I dislike in a person.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，他身上有我讨厌的一切。

sentences.en: That's, I mean, that's quite, I know that's quite strong.
sentences.zh: 这，我的意思是，这挺，我知道这话说得很重。

sentences.en: So let's tease this out.
sentences.zh: 那我们来深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: What do you not like about?
sentences.zh: 你讨厌他什么？

sentences.en: I don't like beards.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌胡子。

sentences.en: Long hair.
sentences.zh: 长发。

sentences.en: I don't like, I mean, to me, the hypocrisy is, it's incredibly glaring.
